content: Gemifloxacin is a quinolone antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication should be taken by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. It is important to take this medication at evenly spaced intervals and to complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Before starting gemifloxacin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other quinolone antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Gemifloxacin may cause a condition affecting the heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can increase the risk of serious irregular heartbeats. The risk may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase this risk. Quinolone antibiotics, including gemifloxacin, may cause serious and potentially permanent tendon damage (e.g., tendinitis, tendon rupture), nerve problems in the arms and legs (peripheral neuropathy), and nervous system issues. Tendon damage can occur during or after treatment. If you experience joint, muscle, or tendon pain or swelling, stop exercising, rest, and seek medical attention immediately. This medication may also worsen a muscle condition called myasthenia gravis. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, or trouble sleeping. While these effects are usually mild, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, gemifloxacin may cause a severe intestinal condition (Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea) during or after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. A mild rash is a common side effect, especially in women under 40 or those on hormone replacement therapy, or when the medication is taken for more than seven days. However, it is important to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. Gemifloxacin may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, particularly in individuals with diabetes. Monitor your blood sugar regularly and report any symptoms of high blood sugar (e.g., increased thirst or urination) or low blood sugar (e.g., sudden sweating, shaking, fast heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands/feet). Carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar, or use quick sources of sugar like candy or fruit juice if necessary. Inform your doctor immediately about any reactions. This medication may make you dizzy, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Gemifloxacin may also increase sensitivity to sunlight, so limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing outdoors. Live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine) may not work effectively while using gemifloxacin. Children may be at greater risk for joint or tendon problems when using this drug. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk in small amounts, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Take gemifloxacin at least two hours before or three hours after taking products that may interfere with its effectiveness, such as quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals (e.g., iron, zinc), and products containing magnesium or aluminum (e.g., antacids). Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory tests (e.g., kidney function, complete blood count, blood sugar, cultures) may be performed before and during treatment to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
